original_question: Given lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), construct families {f_{lambda,a}} of formally linearizable germs with diagonal linear part diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) such that holomorphic linearizability is equivalent to the multivariable Brjuno condition sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))<+infinity; in particular, decide this equivalence for two-dimensional quadratic perturbations f(z)=(lambda_1 z_1, lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z) in the non-resonant case.
target_in_paper: Section 3.7, Open Problem OP18, read together with Definition 17, Definition 18, and Theorem 17. This is the exact match because your draft asks for families {f_{lambda,a}} and repeats the paper's specific 2-dimensional quadratic test case verbatim in substance. OP18 is also explicitly introduced there as a recasting of the paper's first open problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the essential content of OP18: fixing an eigenvalue vector lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), asking for families of formally linearizable germs with diagonal linear part diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), using the multivariable Brjuno series from condition (8), and isolating the paper's highlighted 2-dimensional case f(z)=(lambda_1 z_1, lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
missing_details: The ambient category should be stated explicitly: the paper works in End(C^n,O), i.e. germs of holomorphic self-maps of C^n fixing the origin O, over the field C. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

The family is indexed by an abstract parameter set M, and the intended quantifier is pointwise in the parameter: for each fixed lambda and each a in M, the germ f_{lambda,a} should be holomorphically linearizable if and only if lambda satisfies condition (8). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

Formally linearizable and holomorphically linearizable should be made explicit as formal or holomorphic conjugacy, respectively, to the linear map z |-> diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) z. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

The small-divisor function must be defined precisely: for m>=2, Omega_lambda(m)=min{|lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}-lambda_j| : k_i in N, 2<=k_1+...+k_n<=m, 1<=j<=n, lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}!=lambda_j}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

The general OP18 does not assume non-resonance; rather, it asks for families consisting of formally linearizable germs. Non-resonance appears only in the final 2-dimensional example, where it guarantees formal linearizability automatically by the preceding discussion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
In the special 2-dimensional case, Q must be specified as a pair of quadratic homogeneous polynomials, not just an arbitrary quadratic perturbation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

The non-resonance hypothesis for (lambda_1,lambda_2) should be spelled out: there is no relation lambda_1^{k_1} lambda_2^{k_2}=lambda_j with k_1,k_2 in N, k_1+k_2>=2, and j in {1,2}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

There is no extra nilpotency condition or 'for all sufficiently large m' clause in this problem; the relevant quantifiers are m>=2 in the definition of Omega_lambda and the infinite sum over all k>=0 in condition (8). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
refined_question: Fix n>=1 and lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) in C^n, and for m>=2 define Omega_lambda(m)=min{|lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}-lambda_j| : k_1,...,k_n in N, 2<=k_1+...+k_n<=m, 1<=j<=n, lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}!=lambda_j}. Can one find a parameter space M and a family {f_{lambda,a}}_{a in M} subset End(C^n,O) of holomorphic germs fixing O, each formally conjugate to the linear map z |-> diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) z and satisfying df_{lambda,a}(O)=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), such that for every a in M the germ f_{lambda,a} is holomorphically linearizable if and only if sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))<infinity? In particular, when n=2 and (lambda_1,lambda_2) is non-resonant, is every germ of the form f(z)=(lambda_1 z_1,lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z), with Q=(Q_1,Q_2) a pair of quadratic homogeneous polynomials, holomorphically linearizable if and only if (lambda_1,lambda_2) satisfies that Brjuno condition? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
justification: The draft is aiming at OP18 rather than OP17, because OP18 alone asks to find families {f_{lambda,a}} and then asks exactly the 2-dimensional quadratic-homogeneous question that appears in your draft. Definition 18 supplies the precise meaning of Omega_lambda(m), Theorem 17 supplies the sufficiency of condition (8) that OP18 is trying to turn into an if-and-only-if statement on suitable families, and Definition 17 provides the paper's meaning of resonance/non-resonance. The reference back to OP1 explains why the family-construction language is part of the paper's actual intent, not an added generalization. I leave equivalent_formulation as null because the paper does not prove an equivalent reformulation of OP18; it states it as an open problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))
